proof:
The displayed affine penalty in $z$ is zero at $v$ and at least one at every other binary base. Since $\lambda_i\le1$ on the simplex, each cap strictly misses all foreign fibers. At its own base it takes $\{\lambda_i\ge1/(d+1)\}$, a homothetic simplex of scale $1-1/(d+1)$ about vertex $i$: the inverse subtracts $1/(d+1)$ from the $i$th coordinate and divides all residual coordinates by the scale. Thus its mass is $\gamma_dV$. Some coordinate is at least $1/(d+1)$ at every point of the simplex, which proves closed coverage of all fibers and their boundaries.

The union of the own-fiber hyperplanes $\lambda_i=1/(d+1)$ is volume-null on each fiber. On every positive-mass sign cell, there is consequently an own cap with strictly positive sign; otherwise all $d+1$ coordinates would be strictly below their average. A positive own cap identifies the unique binary base of the cell. Every refinement remains at that base. By pk-w36-menu-strict-sign-consensus the limit is the centroid in each positive cell, retaining the positive sign and all stated fixed-base data. At each positive atom $(v,x)$, then, some $\lambda_i(x)>1/(d+1)$. The closed cap through the atom with margin $\lambda_i(X)-\lambda_i(x)$ minus the same binary penalty captures no foreign fiber and has own mass $(1-\lambda_i(x))^dV<\gamma_d V$. This cap bounds the atom's original raw depth, irrespective of the atom's mass in the output law.

In the unrefined cap-sign partition of two fibers $[0,1]$, there are two isolated half intervals per fiber, each of mass $1/2$. The ordinary centroids of the two cells are $1/4,3/4$. Each original hinge is $\int_0^{1/2}s\,ds=1/8$; it vanishes on the foreign fiber. The isolated through-atom cap toward the nearer endpoint has length $1/4$, giving original normalized depth at most $(1/4)/2=1/8$.
statement:
Let $C=[0,1]^n\times\Delta_d$ for $d\ge1$, with $\Delta_d$ a full simplex of volume $V$ and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Let $\mu$ be summed fiber volume, $M=2^nV$, and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. At each binary base $v$, take the $d+1$ ambient closed caps with margins
$$
L_{v,i}(z,x)=\lambda_i(x)-\frac1{d+1}
-\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\bigl((1-v_\ell)z_\ell+v_\ell(1-z_\ell)\bigr).
$$
These $2^n(d+1)$ caps cover the whole mixed set, each with original mass $\gamma_d M/2^n$. In the strict cap-sign-conditioned midpoint limit of $\mu$, even after any finite max-affine refinement, every positive atom has original mixed depth strictly below $\gamma_d M/2^n$. The output preserves the original cap masses, cap hinges, and every fiberwise joint strict-complement mass and continuous first moment. For $n=d=1$ with $\Delta_1=[0,1]$ and the unrefined cap-sign partition, each original cap mass is $1/2$, each original hinge is $1/8$, and the four output atoms at the two bases have continuous coordinates $1/4$ and $3/4$ and original normalized depths at most $1/8<1/4$.
